title: प्रदेश प्रमुखविहीन बन्यो कोशी : नयाँ नियुक्ति र वैकल्पिक जिम्मेवारी दुवै अनिश्चित
content:
No ads found for this position विराटनगर । पाँचवर्षे कार्यकाल पूरा गरी प्रदेश प्रमुख परशुराम खापुङ बिदा भएसँगै कोशी प्रदेश प्रमुखविहीन बनेको छ। कात्तिक २४ गते खापुङको कार्यकाल विधिवत् रूपमा समाप्त भएपछि नयाँ प्रदेश प्रमुख नियुक्त नहुँदा तथा वैकल्पिक जिम्मेवारीसमेत नतोकिँदा पद रिक्त बनेको हो। कार्यकाल सकिएको यत्तिका दिन बितिसक्दा पनि सरकारले अझै नयाँ प्रदेश प्रमुख पठाउन सकेको छैन। तत्कालीन शेरबहादुर देउवा नेतृत्वको सरकारको सिफारिसमा खापुङ २०७८ साल कात्तिक २५ गते प्रदेश प्रमुखमा नियुक्त भएका थिए। कार्यकालका क्रममा खापुङ विवादमा समेत तानिएका थिए। २०८० असार २२ गते उनले तटस्थ भूमिकामा रहनुपर्ने सभामुख बाबुराम गौतमको समेत हस्ताक्षरलाई मान्यता दिँदै नेपाली कांग्रेसका उद्धव थापालाई पहिलोपटक मुख्यमन्त्रीमा नियुक्त गरेका थिए। तर, सभामुखको हस्ताक्षरसहित बहुमत जुटाइएको उक्त नियुक्ति असंवैधानिक ठहर गर्दै सर्वोच्च अदालतले साउन ११ गते बदर गरिदिएको थियो। नेपालको संविधानको धारा १६५ अनुसार प्रदेश प्रमुखको पदावधि समाप्त भएमा पद रिक्त हुने व्यवस्था छ । त्यस्तै, सोही धाराको उपधारा (२) मा पद रिक्त भएको अवस्थामा नयाँ प्रदेश प्रमुख नियुक्त नभएसम्मका लागि राष्ट्रपतिले अर्को कुनै प्रदेशको प्रदेश प्रमुखलाई उक्त प्रदेशको समेत कामकाज गर्ने गरी तोक्न सक्ने संवैधानिक प्रावधान छ । तर, हालसम्म अन्य कुनै पनि प्रदेशका प्रमुखलाई कोशी प्रदेशको अतिरिक्त जिम्मेवारी दिइएको छैन। संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाअनुसार राष्ट्रपतिले अर्को प्रदेशका प्रमुखलाई अतिरिक्त जिम्मेवारी तोकेको खण्डमा उनले कोशी प्रदेशको मुख्यमन्त्री र मन्त्रीहरूलाई शपथ ग्रहण गराउने, प्रदेश सभाको अधिवेशन आह्वान वा अन्त्य गर्ने तथा विधेयक प्रमाणीकरण गर्ने जस्ता संवैधानिक कार्यहरू सम्पादन गर्नेछन् । यसैबीच, प्रदेश प्रमुखको कार्यालय कोशीकी सूचना अधिकारी सम्पूर्ण थापाले नयाँ प्रदेश प्रमुख तोकिएको बारेमा हालसम्म कार्यालयलाई कुनै आधिकारिक जानकारी प्राप्त नभएको बताइन्। ‘आज सरकारी कार्यालयहरू खुल्ने भएकाले केही जानकारी आउँछ कि भन्ने हो,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘अहिलेसम्म इमेल वा फोनमार्फत प्रदेश प्रमुख तोकिएकोबारे जानकारी आएको छैन।’ Biratnagar. Koshi Province has been left without a chief after the departure of provincial chief Parashuram Khapung after completing his five-year term. The position has become vacant as a new provincial chief has not been appointed and no alternative responsibilities have been assigned since Khapung's term officially ended on Kartik 24. Even after so many days have passed since the end of his term, the government has still not been able to send a new provincial chief. Khapung was appointed as the provincial chief on Kartik 25, 2078 BS, on the recommendation of the then Sher Bahadur Deuba-led government. During his tenure, Khapung was also embroiled in controversy. On July 22, 2001, he appointed Uddhav Thapa of the Nepali Congress as the Chief Minister for the first time, recognizing the signature of Speaker Baburam Gautam, who was supposed to remain neutral. However, the Supreme Court declared the appointment, which had secured a majority with the Speaker's signature, unconstitutional and annulled it on July 11. According to Article 165 of the Constitution of Nepal, the post of the Chief of a Province shall become vacant if the term of office of the Chief of a Province expires . Similarly, in the same article, clause (2) there is a constitutional provision that in the event of a vacancy in the post, the President may designate the Chief of a Province of another Province to also perform the functions of that Province until a new Chief of a Province is appointed . However, so far, no Chief of any other Province has been given the additional responsibility of Koshi Province. According to the constitutional provision, if the President assigns additional responsibilities to the head of another province, he will perform constitutional functions such as administering the oath of office to the Chief Minister and ministers of Koshi Province, convening or adjourning the session of the provincial assembly, and certifying bills . Meanwhile, Sampurna Thapa, information officer at the provincial chief's office in Koshi, said that the office has not received any official information about the appointment of a new provincial chief. "We will have to wait and see if any information will come as government offices will be opened today," she said. "So far, we have not received any information about the appointment of a provincial chief through email or phone."

Koshi Province has been left without a chief after the departure of provincial chief Parashuram Khapung after completing his five-year term. The position has become vacant as a new provincial chief has not been appointed and no alternative responsibilities have been assigned since Khapung's term officially ended on Kartik 24. Even after so many days have passed since the end of his term, the government has still not been able to send a new provincial chief. Khapung was appointed as the provincial chief on Kartik 25, 2078 BS, on the recommendation of the then Sher Bahadur Deuba-led government. During his tenure, Khapung was also embroiled in controversy. On July 22, 2001, he appointed Uddhav Thapa of the Nepali Congress as the Chief Minister for the first time, recognizing the signature of Speaker Baburam Gautam, who was supposed to remain neutral. However, the Supreme Court declared the appointment, which had secured a majority with the Speaker's signature, unconstitutional and annulled it on July 11. According to Article 165 of the Constitution of Nepal, the post of the Chief of a Province shall become vacant if the term of office of the Chief of a Province expires . Similarly, in the same article, clause (2) there is a constitutional provision that in the event of a vacancy in the post, the President may designate the Chief of a Province of another Province to also perform the functions of that Province until a new Chief of a Province is appointed . However, so far, no Chief of any other Province has been given the additional responsibility of Koshi Province. According to the constitutional provision, if the President assigns additional responsibilities to the head of another province, he will perform constitutional functions such as administering the oath of office to the Chief Minister and ministers of Koshi Province, convening or adjourning the session of the provincial assembly, and certifying bills . Meanwhile, Sampurna Thapa, information officer at the provincial chief's office in Koshi, said that the office has not received any official information about the appointment of a new provincial chief. "We will have to wait and see if any information will come as government offices will be opened today," she said. "So far, we have not received any information about the appointment of a provincial chief through email or phone."

Biratnagar. Koshi Province has been left without a chief after the departure of provincial chief Parashuram Khapung after completing his five-year term. The position has become vacant as a new provincial chief has not been appointed and no alternative responsibilities have been assigned since Khapung's term officially ended on Kartik 24. Even after so many days have passed since the end of his term, the government has still not been able to send a new provincial chief. Khapung was appointed as the provincial chief on Kartik 25, 2078 BS, on the recommendation of the then Sher Bahadur Deuba-led government. During his tenure, Khapung was also embroiled in controversy. On July 22, 2001, he appointed Uddhav Thapa of the Nepali Congress as the Chief Minister for the first time, recognizing the signature of Speaker Baburam Gautam, who was supposed to remain neutral. However, the Supreme Court declared the appointment, which had secured a majority with the Speaker's signature, unconstitutional and annulled it on July 11. According to Article 165 of the Constitution of Nepal, the post of the Chief of a Province shall become vacant if the term of office of the Chief of a Province expires . Similarly, in the same article, clause (2) there is a constitutional provision that in the event of a vacancy in the post, the President may designate the Chief of a Province of another Province to also perform the functions of that Province until a new Chief of a Province is appointed . However, so far, no Chief of any other Province has been given the additional responsibility of Koshi Province. According to the constitutional provision, if the President assigns additional responsibilities to the head of another province, he will perform constitutional functions such as administering the oath of office to the Chief Minister and ministers of Koshi Province, convening or adjourning the session of the provincial assembly, and certifying bills . Meanwhile, Sampurna Thapa, information officer at the provincial chief's office in Koshi, said that the office has not received any official information about the appointment of a new provincial chief. "We will have to wait and see if any information will come as government offices will be opened today," she said. "So far, we have not received any information about the appointment of a provincial chief through email or phone."
